Name: Richard Lobb
Question: When referring to a name of something like "Fort Nisqually", if I refer to it later as the Fort, is "Fort" capitalized?
Answer: “Fort Nisqually” is a proper noun and is capped, whereas “the fort” is a common noun and lower case. Sometimes you will see common nouns capitalized, as when the Dewey Cheatham and Howe law firm refers to itself as The Firm, or Old Ivy University calls itself the University, but that’s just an affectation. Common nouns are not capitalized.
